newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt spending to rise in 1997 - parliament.
newsitem.headline: French govt spending to rise in 1997 - parliament.

text.p: The French parliament's finance committee said on Wednesday that it estimated government spending could rise in 1997 by 0.81 percent or 1.38 percent, depending on the method of calculation used.
Philippe Auberger, head of the committee, added that a third method, chosen by the government, yielded a spending increase of 0.06 percent in 1997.
Auberger did not say one method was better than the others and added that whatever calculation was used, the French government's rate of spending increase was slowing.
"The spending slowdown is indisputable, no one believed it could happen," Auberger told journalists.
The government has promised to freeze spending at 1996 levels in current terms in next year's budget.

Separately, the finance committee rejected an amendment proposed by Francois Leotard, member of the junior coalition party UDF, which would have progressively lowered the value added tax (VAT) (sales tax) rate to 19 percent in January 1999 from 20.6 percent.
The committee earlier rejected an amendment suggested by the socialist party that would have cut the VAT to 18.6 percent from January 1997.
